stage.instructions: Classify the element by its main role in the hourglass pipeline. Use path, kind, and summary together; choose one dominant stage.

criteria.prep: Find or rank inputs, scope, work items, or routes before a plan exists.
criteria.condense: Reduce gathered context into a brief, signatures, or bounded evidence set.
criteria.waist: Confirm or amend a plan; decide sufficiency, verdict, or escalation.
criteria.dispatch: Carry out accepted work: apply edits, write outputs, batch tasks, or isolate locks.
criteria.adjudicate: Check outcomes or claims against tests, gates, audits, ledger, or consent rules.
criteria.cross_cutting: Support multiple stages through shared config, budgets, trust, or surfaces.

brief_treatment.instructions: Choose the main evidence form a downstream expensive model needs. Preserve only decision-relevant facts and provenance.

criteria.signature: A function, class, or schema signature is enough; implementation bodies are unnecessary.
criteria.cited_window: Include a hash-pinned source excerpt when exact code, policy, protocol, or contract wording matters.
criteria.failure_evidence: Include relevant test or gate output when the claim concerns observed behavior.
criteria.grounded_claim: State a concrete claim and cite its source path, section, or line.
criteria.exclude_raw: When raw contents should not cross the boundary, omit file, ledger, or credential text and give a safe summary.

handling.instructions: Choose the least capable tier that can safely make the likely edit. Judge required context and risk, not item size.

criteria.code_owned: No model edit is needed: exact mechanical facts or steps can be computed in code without semantic judgment.
criteria.scout: One bounded mechanical change, such as a rename, typo fix, or narrow file-local edit.
criteria.standard: Routine implementation or refactor requires context across files.
criteria.frontier: Architecture, safety, protocol, or waist-level judgment makes mistakes costly.

score.instructions: Rate how much this element matters to the repo-wide waist decision, not how prominent its name looks.
levels: background: omit from a tight brief unless a specific goal reaches it.
notable: include when the current goal touches or depends on it.
central: include in every repo-wide waist brief; it shapes policy, contracts, or outcomes.

waist_relevant.instructions: Would omitting this weaken repo-wide plan confirmation or change its decision? Answer from evidence in state.
waist_relevant.true: Yes: core policy, contract, implementation, or evidence is required; cite its source.
waist_relevant.false: No: peripheral, redundant, or the same evidence is covered elsewhere.

parallel_safe.instructions: Could workers edit in parallel safely? Use known ownership and overlap, never element size.
parallel_safe.true: Yes: work has separate files or state and no dependency between results.
parallel_safe.false: No: edits overlap files or shared state, or depend on another unfinished result.
